title: PEARL: Solver-in-the-Loop Interactive Optimization Modeling from Natural Language
claim: Our compact model matches or beats far larger models, so accuracy does not require scale.
layout: 1 wide scatter plot, categorical scale x-axis, dashed line at our accuracy
description: A single wide scatter plot. The x-axis is reported model scale in categories: 4B, 7B, 8B, 32B, 235B, 685B and Undisclosed. The y-axis is macro-averaged Pass@1 in percent, from about 20 to 75. Each point is a model, shown as a circular logo with a rotated name label and a smaller backbone subtitle. The logos include Qwen, OptMATH, SIRL, ORLM, DeepSeek and GPT. PEARL (Qwen3-4B) is at the top left, in bold, at about 70%. A dashed orange horizontal line runs from it across the plot to show that the large models, such as DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-5, reach only a similar level. A faint blue shaded band with curved contour lines suggests a size-versus-accuracy trend. A small footnote at the bottom right says parameter count is shown when publicly disclosed.
caption: {Macro-averaged Pass@1 versus reported model scale across representative optimization-modeling methods. PEARL (Ours) uses a 4B backbone yet matches or exceeds much larger general-purpose models such as DeepSeek-V3.2-685B, highlighting that solver-mediated interaction and optimization-specific training can deliver strong accuracy in a compact model regime that is more practical for repeated agentic invocation [ref].}
abstract: Optimization modeling is the process of translating real-world decision problems, often described in natural language, into formal mathematical formulations and executable solver code. While recent advances in large language models have shown promise in automating this process, many approaches focus on one-shot generation or rely on predefined execution-and-repair workflows, without explicitly learning a policy for tool use and revision. This stands in sharp contrast to real-world optimization modeling, which is inherently interactive and proceeds through repeated solve-debug-revise cycles. We introduce PEARL, a system for multi-turn solver-interactive optimization modeling that uses Python execution and mathematical programming solvers inside this loop. Rather than relying on a fixed repair workflow, PEARL learns when to test partial models, how to revise from solver diagnostics, and when to stop. It operates in a multi-turn tool-integrated setting where intermediate execution results, feasibility signals, and solution checks are used to improve both formulations and solver code before finalization. Across diverse optimization benchmarks, PEARL substantially improves executable objective agreement over the same-scale base model and is competitive with strong one-shot and tool-augmented baselines. Notably, PEARL-Qwen3-4B outperforms the much larger DeepSeek-V3.2-685B baseline under direct prompting on both macro- and micro-averaged Pass@1. Code and datasets are provided at https://github.com/AuroraLHL/PEARL.
